questions.stem: To which modelling family does Data Vault belong?
questions.explanation: Data Vault belongs to the family of Ensemble Data Modelling, alongside Focal Point and Anchor Modelling.

questions.stem: How should terms such as "Business Vault" and "Raw Vault" be understood?
options: As extensions within the single core Data Vault model, not distinct systems
As Kimball's names for data marts
As Inmon's layers of the EDW
As deprecated names for star schemas
questions.explanation: There is only one Data Vault methodology; Business Vault and Raw Vault are extensions within the same foundational framework, not separate systems.

questions.stem: What do Hub tables store in Data Vault?
options: Business keys that uniquely identify entities, without descriptive information
Stable domain values such as status codes
questions.explanation: Hubs store business keys such as Customer ID or Product ID, organising data by core business concept without storing descriptive information.

questions.stem: What is the role of Link tables in Data Vault?
options: To manage relationships between entities by linking hub tables through foreign keys
To cache the latest state of each hub
questions.explanation: Links capture connections between hubs through foreign keys, allowing the model to evolve as relationships change or new relationships are discovered.

questions.stem: What do Satellite tables contain in Data Vault?
options: Descriptive attributes related to hub entities, separated from the core keys
questions.explanation: Satellites hold contextual information such as names or details, separated from hub keys so descriptive data can be updated without affecting relationships or business keys.

questions.stem: Which Data Vault table type stores stable domain values such as loan status codes and is optional but recommended?
questions.explanation: Reference tables store stable domain values such as status codes or product categories, ensuring consistency and reducing redundancy across the warehouse.

questions.stem: In the layered data architecture described with Data Vault, which layer does Data Vault replace?
options: 3NF modelling in the Transform Zone's Warehousing Layer
Dimensional modelling in the Semantic Layer
questions.explanation: Data Vault replaces Inmon's 3NF approach in the Warehousing Layer of the Transform Zone, while dimensional modelling remains in the Semantic Layer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the options named for adding a Semantic Layer on top of Data Vault?
options: A virtual semantic layer with on-the-fly joins across hubs, links and satellites
Physical tables that pre-aggregate frequently accessed data
A hierarchical tree of parent–child pointers
A dimensional model that simplifies reporting for end users
Leaving the Data Vault structure intact in the Warehousing Layer while serving dimensional views
questions.explanation: The semantic layer options are a virtual layer, physical pre-aggregated tables and dimensional models; hierarchical pointer trees are not among them.

questions.stem: Which fields make a Data Vault satellite bi-temporal by default?
questions.explanation: ValidFrom/ValidTo capture business reality and LoadDate captures when the system recorded it; all three fields together make Data Vault a bi-temporal framework by default.

questions.stem: In the Data Vault loan example, what happens when a loan's interest rate changes from 7.5% to 8.0%?
options: The Hub_Loan row is updated with the new rate
The old rate is deleted from Sat_LoanDetails
A new hub is created for the new rate
The old value stays in Sat_LoanDetails with its validity range and a new row is added, preserving full history
questions.explanation: The old value remains in the satellite with its validity range and a new row is added, so a regulator can ask which rate was valid as of a given date and get an answer.
